title: The One World Schoolhouse: Education Reimagined
author: Salman Khan
note: Mandatory Karpathy review. Adult account of education design and technology adoption, not a children's textbook, parenting guide or technical teaching curriculum. Global application is central despite US examples; T11=0. Educational organization rather than politics is central; T12=0. Specialist reception is mixed: Gunes is positive, Coulson endorses mastery learning but criticizes omitted institutional incentives, and McCarthy and colleagues dispute educational expertise and extrapolation. Those criticisms limit the assessment; the inspected abstracts and reviews do not establish a foundational V9 veto with high confidence. Reform proposal is not partisan mobilization. Not selected as expert consensus praise.
notes: Founder experience supports the origin story; claims of broad educational improvement exceed comparative evidence inspected.
Connects software, classroom time and learning pace, with weak treatment of incentives and governance identified by Coulson.
Mastery thresholds and separating instruction from practice provide reusable design questions.
Explains feedback and gaps in prerequisite knowledge; outcomes are not rigorously causally tested here.
D=6, moderate confidence from Gunes, Coulson and Kirkus reviews. Development cases add learning; familiar criticism of schooling and broad proposals reduce yield. No full-text audit.
Learning design remains relevant, but the platform snapshot and revolutionary framing have aged.
Technology-enabled scaling and institutional improvement fit; little deep computing or industrial analysis.
Direct founder experience, but education specialists dispute parts of the synthesis.
Personal development and reform ideas give an accessible structure.
Clear expression with promotional overstatement.

title: Mental Models: 30 Thinking Tools that Separate the Average from the Exceptional
author: Peter Hollins
note: Mandatory Karpathy review; not selected on expert acclaim. The named 30-model work is distinct from the author's 16-model sequel and other titles. Publisher description and licensed sample show decision heuristics as the principal payload, rather than spirituality or emotional life support. It is not a specialist curriculum; H3 and V7 are not inferred from the self-help label. Generalization and shallow treatment lower the score. The heading about ignoring black swans is not by itself evidence of a foundational falsehood. No serious veto established from inspected evidence.
notes: Familiar concepts are presented as broad rules; empirical validation and boundary conditions are thin in inspected material.
Several disciplines appear, but there is little sustained integration into a system.
A usable checklist of reasoning prompts, mostly familiar to a quantitative reader.
Short descriptions give limited causal depth or explanation of failure conditions.

title: Hot Seat: The Startup CEO Guidebook
author: Dan Shapiro
note: Mandatory Karpathy review. Retained under H7's explicit exception for organizing skilled technical work: startup formation, funding, delegation and exit constraints form the overall subject. Hiring, pitches and negotiation are components rather than the dominant isolated purpose. H3 is not established: this is an explanatory practitioner account of organizational decisions, not technical proficiency training, despite checklists and a guidebook title. US venture-backed company practice predominates, T11=-10. Finance supports the broader company lifecycle rather than dominating it, T12=0. No serious veto established; survivorship and anecdotal selection limit evidence.
notes: Direct experience and named company cases are useful, but selected founder stories do not establish general causal laws.
Links ownership, financing, team structure, product strategy and acquisition incentives.
Concrete tradeoffs about cofounders and control can transfer to other technical ventures.
Explains incentive conflicts and constraints; some chapters substitute directives for mechanism.

D=7, moderate confidence from the publisher sample, detailed contents and reader reports. Distinct lifecycle decisions add learning; pitch templates and familiar personnel advice have lower yield for this collection.
Organizational conflicts endure; financing conventions and platform-specific advice date.
Good technical-organization fit, little explanation of engineering itself.
Experienced founder, with limited independent specialist review inspected.

title: You Have the Right to Remain Innocent
author: James J. Duane
note: Mandatory Karpathy review. Public legal argument illustrated by wrongful-conviction cases, not specialist legal training or a routine communication manual. H3/H7 do not apply on this characterization. US institutional risks and civil liberties dominate, T11=-10; state power is central, T12=-10. The historical legal snapshot must not be treated as current jurisdiction-specific advice. No partisan recruitment or serious epistemic veto established. The book's narrow recommendation still has transferable information-asymmetry and institutional-incentive content, so V3 is not established.
notes: Case records and legal expertise support the argument; selection emphasizes failures and is not an estimate of their prevalence.
Connects interrogation, evidence rules and incentives within a narrow national system.
Useful asymmetric-risk reasoning; direct legal applicability is jurisdiction-bound.
Shows how innocent statements and incentives can produce adverse outcomes.
D=6, moderate confidence from Kirkus, contents and reader reports. Distinct failure cases teach mechanisms, but repeated restatement of a small advice set adds limited yield.
Institutional risk remains relevant; legal details require updating.
Institutional power fits peripherally; almost no technology or industry.
Law professor with relevant expertise and a published law-journal review; the latter is student-authored.
Short and accessible, with a clear central argument.
Forceful prose can flatten differences between situations.
